subject: Wuyts et al. (2002)
object: Wuyts et al. (2002) described a boy with multiple exostoses, hypertrichosis, mental retardation, and epilepsy, along with brain abnormalities, caused by a de novo submicroscopic interstitial deletion of chromosome 8q24. Molecular analysis showed that the deleted region overlapped the Langer-Giedion syndrome region and included the EXT1 gene and additional genes distal to EXT1. The deletion probably did not include the TRPS1 gene, which lies proximal to EXT1.

subject: Deardorff et al. (2012)
object: Deardorff et al. (2012) reported that children with RAD21 mutations had growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlapped those of Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS). Unlike children with mutations in NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3, these individuals had much milder cognitive impairment than those with classic CdLS.

subject: Deardorff et al. (2012)
object: Deardorff et al. (2012) showed that human mutations in RAD21, an integral structural protein of the cohesin complex, cause a congenital phenotype consistent with a cohesinopathy. They suggested that dominant missense mutations result in more severe functional defects and worse structural and cognitive clinical findings than loss-of-function mutations.

subject: Deardorff et al. (2012)
object: Deardorff et al. (2012) suggested that, compared to RAD21 loss-of-function mutations, dominant missense mutations cause more severe functional defects and worse structural and cognitive clinical findings.

subject: Deardorff et al. (2012)
object: Deardorff et al. (2012) found that the RAD21 mutations act at the interface between RAD21 and the other cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A, and that they impair the cellular DNA damage response.

subject: Deardorff et al. (2012)
object: Deardorff et al. (2012) showed in a zebrafish model that the RAD21 mutations disrupted transcription.

subject: Minor et al. (2014)
object: Minor et al. (2014) reported 2 patients with atypical Cornelia de Lange syndrome and RAD21 mutations. The first patient had developmental delay, hypospadias, inguinal hernia, and dysmorphic features. The second patient had developmental delay, characteristic facial features, hirsutism, and hand and foot anomalies. The first patient was more mildly affected than the second.

subject: Minor et al. (2014)
object: In a patient with mild atypical Cornelia de Lange syndrome, Minor et al. (2014) identified an in-frame intragenic deletion of exon 13 of the RAD21 gene. The deletion was inherited from the patient's mother, who had a history of melanoma and other unspecified medical problems. The authors described this as the first familial case.

subject: Minor et al. (2014)
object: In a patient with atypical Cornelia de Lange syndrome, Minor et al. (2014) identified a c.592_593dup frameshift mutation in the RAD21 gene.

subject: Minor et al. (2014)
object: Minor et al. (2014) discussed variable clinical presentation within families and low penetrance of RAD21 mutations. They emphasized the clinical utility of RAD21 mutation analysis in patients with atypical forms of CdLS, as well as molecular genetic testing in mildly affected patients.

subject: Pereza et al. (2015)
object: Pereza et al. (2015) revised their earlier diagnosis of Langer-Giedion syndrome in a girl with a 7.5-Mb interstitial deletion at 8q23.3q24.13. The deletion included EXT1 but not TRPS1. Because it also included RAD21 and 30 other RefSeq genes, the authors suggested that the correct diagnosis was Cornelia de Lange syndrome-4. They compared her with other reported patients who had CDLS4 caused by heterozygous 8q24 deletions.

subject: Boyle et al. (2017)
object: In a patient with Cornelia de Lange syndrome (individual IV.16), Boyle et al. (2017) identified a novel heterozygous 1-bp deletion (c.704delG) in the RAD21 gene, predicted to result in a frameshift and premature stop codon (p.Ser235IlefsTer19) with a deleterious effect. The deletion was also found in the patient's mother and 2 aunts, none of whom had been suspected of having CdLS or a cohesinopathy before the study.

subject: Boyle et al. (2017)
object: Boyle et al. (2017) reported intrafamilial phenotypic variation in a family segregating a RAD21 deletion: the index patient could be classified as having mild CdLS, whereas the mother and 2 aunts carrying the variant did not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for CdLS. The authors suggested that, together with previous reports, this indicates incomplete penetrance associated with RAD21 variants and that such individuals may be underdiagnosed.

subject: Gudmundsson et al. (2019)
object: Gudmundsson et al. (2019) reported a 15-month-old boy with developmental delay, distinct CdLS-like facial features, gastrointestinal reflux in early infancy, testis retention, prominent digit pads, and diaphragmatic hernia, which the authors concluded expanded the clinical description of CdLS type 4.

subject: Gudmundsson et al. (2019)
object: In a 15-month-old boy with CdLS type 4, Gudmundsson et al. (2019) identified by exome sequencing a de novo heterozygous 3-bp deletion in the RAD21 gene (c.1774_1776del), resulting in deletion of gln592 (p.Gln592del); the variant was absent from both healthy parents and was predicted to be disease-causing. In silico structural modeling predicted that the deletion disrupts contact between RAD21 lys591 and SMC1A residues glu1191 and glu1192, altering the RAD21-SMC1A interface.

subject: Kruszka et al. (2019)
object: Kruszka et al. (2019) reported 4 individuals with holoprosencephaly who had variants in the non-X-linked cohesin complex genes SMC3 and RAD21. They also reported variants in the X-linked cohesin genes STAG2 and SMC1A in 11 other individuals with holoprosencephaly. The authors concluded that the cohesin complex is an important regulator of median forebrain development.

subject: Dorval et al. (2020)
object: Dorval et al. (2020) reported a boy with a mild Cornelia de Lange syndrome presentation and a molecularly confirmed novel RAD21 mutation. They compared his clinical features with those of previously described patients carrying different RAD21 intragenic mutations to further delineate the phenotype. They noted that RAD21 is associated with a milder phenotype.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations (24 different intragenic sequence variants and 7 unique microdeletions), including 24 previously unpublished cases, from Australia, Europe, Turkey, Canada and the United States. Full clinical information was available for 29 individuals from 22 families (cohort A). All of them had CdLS clinical scores of at least 5. Their phenotype was an attenuated CdLS phenotype compared with that caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, with milder facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition and behavior.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) found that in the 29 cohort A patients with RAD21 variants, the frequent features were short nose (23/26), long and/or smooth philtrum (26/29), concave nasal ridge (24/29), thick eyebrows (20/24), long eyelashes (21/26), synophrys (19/28), thin upper lip vermilion (23/29), short fifth finger (23/28), postnatal microcephaly (16/28) and gastroesophageal reflux (13/25). No patient had major limb malformations (0/29) or visual impairment (0/24). Small hands (5/27), small feet (3/27), hirsutism (10/26) and seizures (2/22) were less common than in the NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts. Hearing loss was present in 8/24, heart defects in 9/23 and cleft palate in 6/25.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) found that cognitive functioning and behavior were attenuated in RAD21 patients: 16 of 29 (55%) had normal or mildly impaired cognition, none had severe or profound disability, and all patients aged 3 years and older used some words. Problems were mainly language-based. Behavioral problems were present in 14 of 25 (56%), mainly anxiety, ADHD, autistic features and obsessive-compulsive behavior. Self-injurious behavior (1/18) and aggression (1/16) were infrequent.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) reported that in RAD21 patients pregnancies and births were usually normal and prenatal growth retardation was uncommon. Short stature and microcephaly developed after birth. About half had congenital anomalies such as cleft palate and cardiac anomalies. Unusual findings included vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut. Diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia or choanal atresia occurred occasionally.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) suggested, from limited data on cohort B, that biallelic RAD21 variants can cause Mungan syndrome and monoallelic RAD21 variants can cause holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics. In several further cases, including cases with sclerocornea, it was uncertain whether the RAD21 variant was involved.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) found 31 different RAD21 alterations in 33 families: 7 unique deletions (6 of which also included other genes) and 24 intragenic sequence variants. Of the sequence variants, 13 were predicted to be truncating (2 nonsense, 2 splice site and 9 frameshift) and were scattered throughout the gene, 3 were in-frame deletions, and the missense variants tended to cluster at the protein-binding domains. Two variants were recurrent (p.Cys585Arg and p.Arg586*). Nine of 21 index cases with known inheritance had familial variants.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) reported a recurrent RAD21 missense variant, c.1753T>C (p.Cys585Arg), in 2 families: it arose de novo in 1 previously reported patient and was found in 2 relatives in a new family. Molecular dynamics modeling predicted that Cys585Arg destabilizes the RAD21-SMC1A domain by causing the adjacent Arg586 to lose its salt-bridge contact with Glu577.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) reported a recurrent RAD21 nonsense variant, c.1756C>T (p.Arg586*), in 2 previously unpublished families. In one family it was inherited from the father, who was also affected. Facial morphology varied between the families carrying this variant.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) updated a family with a 1-bp deletion in RAD21, c.704delG (p.Ser235Ilefs*19), carried by 5 affected members, with CdLS scores of 9 to 12. Facial morphology varied within the family.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) found a de novo in-frame deletion in RAD21, c.1774_1776del (p.Gln592del), in a previously reported patient with a CdLS score of 8. Molecular dynamics simulation predicted that loss of Gln592 distorts an alpha helix and moves Lys605 away from ATPase site 1 of the SMC1A/SMC3 head, disturbing the cohesin cycle.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) found a RAD21 in-frame deletion, c.1800_1802del (p.Phe600del), in a previously unpublished patient with classic CdLS who had no variants in other known CdLS genes on a targeted gene panel. Modeling did not show a structural effect, but the authors considered the variant likely pathogenic based on the phenotype.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) found a de novo RAD21 missense variant, c.1808T>C (p.Leu603Pro), in a previously reported patient in cohort B. Modeling predicted that Pro603 bends the alpha helix and moves Lys605 out of its position near ATPase site 1.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) found a de novo RAD21 missense variant, c.1033T>C (p.Ser345Pro), in a DECIPHER patient. Modeling predicted that it impairs the interaction between RAD21 and STAG1/2 by creating a new curved alpha-helix segment that separates from the STAG2 surface. The previously reported de novo variant c.1127C>G (p.Pro376Arg) was predicted to form a new salt bridge that over-stabilizes the RAD21-STAG2 interaction.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) updated the family with Mungan syndrome in which 3 sibs were homozygous for the RAD21 variant c.1864G>A (p.Ala622Thr). Modeling showed no structural alteration. However, Ala622 lies next to Thr623, a PLK1 phosphorylation site, and earlier zebrafish morpholino studies supported pathogenicity. Heterozygous family members had some CdLS-spectrum features, but it remained uncertain whether the heterozygous variant causes a phenotype.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) reported further previously unpublished heterozygous RAD21 variants in CdLS patients. These were a de novo frameshift c.617_620del (p.Ile206Thrfs*3), a de novo frameshift c.1635del (p.Gly547Alafs*65), a paternally inherited missense variant c.1382C>T (p.Thr461Ile), and a missense variant c.194G>A (p.Arg65Gln) from ClinVar that was reported as a VUS. Based on phenotype, modeling and the literature, the authors considered Arg65Gln and Thr461Ile likely pathogenic, possibly through altered phosphorylation motifs or PDS5 interaction.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) observed a trend toward higher CdLS scores and more frequent growth impairment in patients with microdeletions than in those with intragenic variants, but no difference in major malformations or in cognitive and behavioral problems. CdLS scores did not differ between truncating and nontruncating sequence variants. Variability within and between families was striking, especially in cognition and behavior, and in most families it could not be explained by mosaicism.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) noted that RAD21 variants were frequently familial (familial in 5 of 12 cohort A cases with known inheritance). Mildly affected parents were sometimes diagnosed only after more severely affected offspring were recognized, so the authors recommended parental testing even when parents appear unaffected.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) suggested that the relatively mild phenotype indicates RAD21 is not highly intolerant to loss of function, unlike other CdLS genes. They speculated that RAD21 haploinsufficiency may be compensated more effectively than loss of other cohesin genes, noting that haploinsufficiency gave roughly halved RAD21 RNA without compensatory upregulation.

subject: Krab et al. (2020)
object: Krab et al. (2020) reported that no RAD21 variant would have been missed using the CdLS consensus criteria for molecular testing. CdLS had been suspected before testing in about 60% of index cases (13/21). The authors concluded that the CdLS score remains a reliable tool.

subject: Lei et al. (2020)
object: Lei et al. (2020) described a 6-year-old Han Chinese boy, the first child of healthy unrelated parents, who had a de novo t(8;18)(q22;q21) translocation. He had growth retardation (height and weight -2.0 SD), mild-to-moderate intellectual disability, left-sided cleft palate, and a congenital heart defect (ventricular septal defect, double-outlet right ventricle, and juxtaposition of the aorta and pulmonary artery). He also had thoracic scoliosis, butterfly vertebrae, fifth-finger clinodactyly, fingerpads, umbilical and inguinal hernias, recurrent respiratory infections, and facial dysmorphism including arched thick eyebrows, long eyelashes, a depressed nasal bridge, anteverted nostrils, large prominent ears, dental malocclusion, and micrognathia. Kabuki syndrome was initially suspected, and multiple exostoses were found at age 10 years.

subject: Lei et al. (2020)
object: Lei et al. (2020) used nanopore long-read sequencing and the dnarrange pipeline in this patient. The de novo t(8;18) translocation turned out to be germline chromothripsis: the genome had been shattered into 19 fragments (15 from chromosome 8 and 4 from chromosome 18) that rejoined in random order and orientation. The rearrangement caused 4 deletions on chromosome 8 (456, 1,957, 520, and 3,529 kb) and 1 deletion on chromosome 18 (1,528 kb), all of which were consistent with array results. One chromosome 8 deletion contained RAD21 and EXT1 but not TRPS1. Earlier short-read whole-genome sequencing had not resolved the rearrangement, and no pathogenic variants were found in the Kabuki syndrome genes.

subject: Lei et al. (2020)
object: Lei et al. (2020) found reduced RAD21 and EXT1 expression on quantitative RT-PCR of the patient's lymphoblastoid cells, while TRPS1 expression was unchanged. They concluded that loss of RAD21 and EXT1 explained the phenotype, a likely contiguous gene syndrome combining CdLS4 and atypical Langer-Giedion syndrome. They considered involvement of other disrupted genes, including ZFPM2, unlikely.

subject: Lei et al. (2020)
object: Lei et al. (2020) compared their patient with 5 previously reported patients who had Langer-Giedion syndrome with deletions that included RAD21 and EXT1 but spared TRPS1. The 6 patients shared overlapping features: arched thick eyebrows (6 patients), long eyelashes (5), depressed or broad nasal bridge (5), sparse scalp hair (4), and intellectual disability (4 of 6). Only their patient had thoracic scoliosis and a congenital heart defect. Because 2 of 8 previously reported patients with RAD21 variants had congenital heart disease, the authors suggested that RAD21 deficiency might be responsible for the heart disease.

subject: Goel and Parasivam (2020)
object: Goel and Parasivam (2020) reported another case of holoprosencephaly associated with a loss-of-function variant in the RAD21 gene.

subject: Kruszka (2020)
object: Kruszka (2020) replied to a correspondence that reported another case of holoprosencephaly associated with a RAD21 loss-of-function variant.
